note: Local micro-topics that extend the Marble Skill Taxonomy where it has no coverage of a school's curriculum (US history, civics, maps, science heroes). Same shape as a Marble topic plus `kid` (the 3-option question: q, a, w) and `prereqs` ([[id, 'hard'|'soft'], ...]). Ids start with lt_. Built into public/tax.json by build.mjs. Database ODbL 1.0, text CC BY-SA 4.0 (see LICENSING.md). Standards keys: cas-ss-2022 (Colorado Academic Standards, Social Studies), cas-sc-2020 (Science), ck-seq (Core Knowledge Sequence section, grade 2).

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Map keys and symbols
topics.description: A map key (legend) explains what the map's symbols and colors mean; use it to find places and features, and tell what a map is for (a street map vs a weather map)
evidence: Use a map key to say what a symbol on a map stands for
Tell what kind of map it is and what it is for
topics.assessmentPrompt: Show {{name}} a simple map with a key. Can they use the key to find the school, a river or a park?

kid.q: What does a map key (legend) do?
kid.a: Tells you what the map's symbols mean
w: Tells you what time it is

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Compass rose and directions
topics.description: Use a compass rose to find north, south, east and west, and the in-between directions northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest, to describe where places are on a map
evidence: Point to north, south, east and west on a map using the compass rose
Use an in-between direction like northeast to say where a place is
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a map, can {{name}} say which direction one place is from another, including an in-between direction like southwest?

kid.q: Which direction is between north and east?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Seven continents and five oceans
topics.description: Name and find the seven continents (Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia) and the oceans (Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, Southern) on a map or globe
evidence: Name the seven continents
Find the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans on a globe
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name the seven continents and point to the Pacific Ocean on a globe?

kid.q: How many continents are there?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Equator, hemispheres and poles
topics.description: The equator is an imaginary line around the middle of Earth that splits it into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres; the North and South Poles are at the top and bottom; the Prime Meridian splits Eastern and Western Hemispheres
evidence: Point to the equator and the two poles on a globe
Say which hemisphere the United States is in
topics.assessmentPrompt: On a globe, can {{name}} find the equator and the poles and say that we live in the Northern Hemisphere?

kid.q: What is the equator?
kid.a: An imaginary line around the middle of Earth
w: A mountain at the North Pole

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Landform words
topics.description: Know geography words for the shapes of land and water: coast, valley, prairie, desert, oasis, peninsula, island, bay, harbor, mountain, plain; use them to describe places like Colorado's mountains and plains
evidence: Match words like valley, peninsula and prairie to pictures
Describe the land near home with the right words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain the difference between an island and a peninsula, or a valley and a prairie?

kid.q: Land with water on three sides is a ___.

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Our place: Colorado, the U.S. and its neighbors
topics.description: Name your city, state (Colorado), country (United States) and continent (North America); find Canada and Mexico as the United States' neighbors, and the Rocky Mountains, Mississippi River and Great Lakes on a map
evidence: Name city, state, country and continent in order
Find Canada and Mexico on a map of North America
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say that Boulder is in Colorado, in the United States, in North America, and name the two countries next to the U.S.?

kid.q: Which country is north of the United States?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The Constitution: We the People
topics.description: The Constitution is the highest law of the United States; it begins 'We the People' because the government gets its power from the people; James Madison is called the Father of the Constitution
evidence: Say what the Constitution is (the highest law of our land)
Explain why it starts with 'We the People'
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain that the Constitution is the rule book for the whole country and that its power comes from the people?

kid.q: What is the Constitution?
kid.a: The highest law of the United States

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The War of 1812
topics.description: In 1812 the United States went to war with Britain: British ships were taking American sailors (impressment); the warship Old Ironsides won sea battles; the British burned the White House, and Dolley Madison saved George Washington's portrait; James Madison was president
evidence: Name one reason the War of 1812 started
Tell what Dolley Madison saved when the White House burned
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of the British burning the White House and what Dolley Madison rescued?

kid.q: Who was president during the War of 1812?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Fort McHenry and The Star-Spangled Banner
topics.description: During the War of 1812, Francis Scott Key watched the British attack Fort McHenry all night; at dawn the American flag still flew, and he wrote the poem that became our national anthem, The Star-Spangled Banner
evidence: Say who wrote The Star-Spangled Banner and what he saw
Explain what a national anthem is
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why the words 'the flag was still there' mattered to Francis Scott Key?

kid.q: What did Francis Scott Key write after the battle at Fort McHenry?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Immigration: coming to America
topics.description: An immigrant is a person who moves to a new country to live; millions came to America for freedom, safety or a better life, many arriving by ship at Ellis Island past the Statue of Liberty; the motto 'e pluribus unum' means 'out of many, one'
evidence: Say what an immigrant is and one reason people immigrate
Tell what Ellis Island and the Statue of Liberty meant to newcomers
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what an immigrant is and why so many people came to America?

kid.q: What is an immigrant?
kid.a: A person who moves to a new country to live

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Fighting for a cause: equal rights
topics.description: America says all people are created equal, but not everyone has always been treated equally; many brave people worked peacefully to change unfair laws and win equal rights for all, and that work is called fighting for a cause
evidence: Explain what equal rights means in kid words
Name one person who fought for a cause
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what it means to fight for a cause and give an example of a right people have won?

kid.q: Fighting for a cause means working to ___.

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Rosa Parks and Martin Luther King Jr.
topics.description: Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, which started a bus boycott; Martin Luther King Jr. led peaceful marches and gave the 'I Have a Dream' speech about equal rights for all
evidence: Tell what Rosa Parks did on the bus and why it mattered
Say what Martin Luther King Jr.'s dream was about
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of Rosa Parks and the bus boycott, and say what Dr. King dreamed of?

kid.q: What did Rosa Parks refuse to do?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Jackie Robinson and Cesar Chavez
topics.description: Jackie Robinson became the first Black player in modern Major League Baseball in 1947 and faced unfair treatment with courage; Cesar Chavez led farm workers to win fair pay and safer work through peaceful strikes and boycotts
evidence: Say why Jackie Robinson was important
Say who Cesar Chavez helped and how
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jackie Robinson was first at, and who Cesar Chavez stood up for?

kid.q: Cesar Chavez helped which workers get fair treatment?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Susan B. Anthony, Eleanor Roosevelt and Mary McLeod Bethune
topics.description: Susan B. Anthony worked so women could vote; Eleanor Roosevelt spoke up for civil and human rights around the world; Mary McLeod Bethune started a school so Black students could get an education
evidence: Say what Susan B. Anthony wanted for women
Say what Mary McLeod Bethune built and why
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} match each of these three women to the cause she fought for?

kid.q: Susan B. Anthony fought for women's right to ___.

topics.subject: History
topics.name: What government does
topics.description: A government makes and enforces laws, keeps people safe, settles disagreements and provides services like police and fire protection, roads, schools, parks and snow removal; it is a bit like the rules and helpers of a family or school
evidence: Name two things a government does
Name a service the city or state provides
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name some jobs a government does, like making laws or plowing snowy roads?

kid.q: Which is a job of government?
kid.a: Making laws and keeping people safe

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Leaders: mayor, governor, president
topics.description: Communities have leaders at different levels: a mayor leads a city, a governor leads a state (Colorado) and the president leads the country; good leaders listen, are fair and honest, and help the group reach its goals
evidence: Match mayor, governor and president to city, state and country
Name one quality of a good leader
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say who leads a city, a state and the country, and what makes a leader good?

kid.q: Who leads a whole state like Colorado?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Being a citizen
topics.description: A citizen is a full member of a country, by being born there or by becoming one later (naturalization); citizens have rights, like voting and holding office, and responsibilities, like following laws, paying taxes and helping the community
evidence: Say one right and one responsibility of a citizen
Explain two ways a person can become a U.S. citizen
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what a citizen is and name a right and a responsibility citizens have?

kid.q: Which is a responsibility of a citizen?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Making your community better
topics.description: People improve their school and community by volunteering, cleaning up, helping neighbors, and sharing ideas respectfully (speaking up, writing letters, voting when grown up); solving problems together makes a community stronger
evidence: Name two ways to help your school or community
Say a respectful way to share an idea you disagree about
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} name something they could do to make school or the neighborhood better, and a respectful way to share an idea?

kid.q: Which helps your community?
kid.a: Volunteering to clean up a park

topics.subject: Life Skills
topics.name: Scarcity: not enough for everyone
topics.description: Scarcity means there is not enough of something (money, time, water, cookies) for everyone to have all they want, so people must choose; goods are things you can buy and services are jobs people do for you
evidence: Explain scarcity with an example
Sort examples into goods and services
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why we can't have everything we want (scarcity) and give an example of a good and a service?

kid.q: Scarcity means there is ___ of something for everyone.

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Science heroes
topics.description: Scientists and inventors who changed the world: Anton van Leeuwenhoek built microscopes and saw tiny living things; Elijah McCoy invented an oil cup that kept train engines running (the real McCoy); Florence Nightingale made hospitals clean and safe; Daniel Hale Williams performed one of the first heart surgeries
evidence: Match each science hero to what they did
Say why one of their discoveries still matters today
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say what Leeuwenhoek saw with his microscope, or how Florence Nightingale changed hospitals?

kid.q: What did Anton van Leeuwenhoek use to see tiny living things?

topics.subject: Science
topics.name: Earth is a magnet: how a compass works
topics.description: Earth acts like a giant magnet with magnetic poles near the North and South Poles; a compass needle is a small magnet that turns to point north, so you can find directions outdoors (orienteering)
evidence: Explain why a compass needle points north
Use a compass to find north and then east
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a compass needle always swings to point north?

kid.q: A compass needle points north because ___.
kid.a: Earth acts like a giant magnet
